question: When an existing SQLite database has no subagent rows or migration receipt but a legacy `runs.json` remains, should doctor only preserve and warn, or provide an explicit operator-confirmed import/archive recovery action?
rationale: Source state alone cannot distinguish a legitimate never-imported registry from stale data left by the previously shipped post-commit cleanup failure, so either automatic choice can lose current state or resurrect old runs.

options.title: Preserve automatically, recover explicitly
options.body: Skip ambiguous automatic import but offer a clear operator-confirmed doctor action to import or archive the preserved source, with upgrade and replay tests.

options.title: Preserve and warn only
options.body: Accept that ambiguous legacy records remain inaccessible until maintainers or support resolve the source manually.

options.title: Continue automatic import
options.body: Favor legacy-state recovery but accept that stale files from the old cleanup boundary can resurrect deleted runs.

recommendation.title: Preserve automatically, recover explicitly
recommendation.body: Skip ambiguous automatic import but offer a clear operator-confirmed doctor action to import or archive the preserved source, with upgrade and replay tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior originates in the SQLite subagent persistence change associated with this owner, including the original legacy import contract.
